[
  "When melanoma is suspected, the entire lesion should be completely excised with a narrow (1‑3 mm) margin to allow histological diagnosis.",
  "Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as facial lesions (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions, and genital lesions.",
  "The consensus rate for the recommendation that incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions is 100 % (21/21).",
  "Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended and first‑line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness and for melanoma in situ.",
  "Surgical margins for melanoma should be based on tumor thickness.",
  "Sentinel lymph node biopsy, when indicated, should be performed before wide excision of the primary tumor and, whenever possible, in the same operative setting.",
  "The clinician should examine the image for an atypical pigment network, which consists of irregular meshes and thickened lines.",
  "The clinician should examine the image for blue areas, which represent regression structures.",
  "Atypical pigment network and blue areas are the only criteria that contribute points to the 7‑point score.",
  "An atypical pigment network is classified as a major risk indicator under the 7‑point checklist.",
  "Blue areas are classified as a minor risk indicator under the 7‑point checklist.",
  "The 7‑point checklist includes both major and minor risk indicators for melanoma assessment."
]
